request: what is a linear combination of two vectors?

beats.intent: A grid with u = (1, 0.5) and v = (-0.5, 1)
beats.narration: Two vectors, u and v.
beats.code:
stage.title("A linear combination")
p = draw_plane(stage)
u = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 0.5), color=YELLOW, label="u")
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (-0.5, 1), color=BLUE, label="v")

beats.intent: u scaled to 2u = (2, 1)
beats.narration: Stretch u to twice its length.
beats.code: scale_vector(stage, p, u, 2)

beats.intent: v added tip to tail after 2u, landing at (1.5, 2), with the result drawn in green
beats.narration: Add v on the end: two u plus v lands at one point five, two. Every point of the plane is some mix like this.
beats.code:
step = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(2, 1), p.c2p(1.5, 2))
w = draw_vector(stage, p, (1.5, 2), color=GREEN, label="2u + v")

request: what does the matrix [[1, 0], [0, 0.5]] do to shapes?

beats.intent: A grid with a unit square and a circle of radius 1
beats.narration: The unit square and a circle on the grid.
beats.code:
stage.title("Squashing vertically")
p = draw_plane(stage)
sq = draw_unit_square(stage, p)
circ = Circle(radius=np.linalg.norm(p.c2p(1, 0) - p.c2p(0, 0)), color=YELLOW).move_to(p.c2p(0, 0))
stage.play(Create(circ))
stage.add(circ)

beats.intent: The matrix applied: everything squashed to half height
beats.narration: Apply the matrix: heights halve, widths stay.
beats.code: apply_matrix(stage, p, [[1, 0], [0, 0.5]], riders=[sq, circ])

beats.intent: The squashed square labelled area 1/2 beside det = 0.5
beats.narration: The square now has area a half, and so does every region: the determinant is one half.
beats.code:
stage.label(sq, "area ½", direction=UP, color=GREEN)
stage.equation(r"\det\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 \end{bmatrix} = 0.5")

request: how can solving two equations be seen as mixing the columns of a matrix?

beats.intent: A grid with the column vectors a1 = (2, 1) and a2 = (1, 3) and the target b = (4, 7)
beats.narration: Solve two x plus y equals four and x plus three y equals seven. The columns are two, one and one, three; the target is four, seven.
beats.code:
stage.title("Ax = b as a mix of columns")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=6, y_extent=8)
a1 = draw_vector(stage, p, (2, 1), color=YELLOW, label="a1")
a2 = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 3), color=BLUE, label="a2")
b = mark_point(stage, p, (4, 7), color=RED, label="b = (4, 7)")

beats.intent: One a1 then two a2 laid tip to tail from the origin, reaching b
beats.narration: Take one of the first column, then two of the second: you arrive exactly at b.
beats.code:
s1 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(2, 1), p.c2p(3, 4))
s2 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(3, 4), p.c2p(4, 7))

beats.narration: So the solution is x equals one, y equals two: the amounts of each column.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"1\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix} + 2\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}4\\7\end{bmatrix}")

request: how do you make a unit vector?

beats.intent: A grid with v = (3, 4) and its length 5 labelled
beats.narration: The vector three, four has length five.
beats.code:
stage.title("A unit vector")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=5, y_extent=5)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (3, 4))
stage.caption("v = (3, 4) has length 5")

beats.intent: v shrunk by 1/5 to (0.6, 0.8), sitting on the unit circle
beats.narration: Divide by its length: it shrinks to point six, point eight, length exactly one.
beats.code:
circ = Circle(radius=np.linalg.norm(p.c2p(1, 0) - p.c2p(0, 0)), color=GREY_B).move_to(p.c2p(0, 0))
stage.play(Create(circ))
stage.add(circ)
scale_vector(stage, p, v, 0.2)
stage.caption("Divided by 5: length 1")

beats.intent: The short vector beside v/|v| = (0.6, 0.8)
beats.narration: Same direction, length one: that is a unit vector.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\frac{v}{|v|} = \frac{(3, 4)}{5} = (0.6, 0.8)")

request: how far is a point from a line?

beats.intent: A grid with the line y = x/2 and the point P = (1, 3)
beats.narration: Here is a line through the origin and a point P above it.
beats.code:
stage.title("Distance to a line")
p = draw_plane(stage)
ln = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(-4, -2), p.c2p(4, 2), color=BLUE)
P = mark_point(stage, p, (1, 3), color=RED, label="P")

beats.intent: The shadow of P on the line: the foot at (2, 1)
beats.narration: Drop P straight onto the line: its shadow lands at two, one.
beats.code: project_vector(stage, p, (1, 3), (2, 1))

beats.intent: The perpendicular from P to the foot drawn in yellow beside its length √5
beats.narration: The shortest distance is that perpendicular: from one, three to two, one, root five long.
beats.code:
perp = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(1, 3), p.c2p(2, 1), color=YELLOW)
stage.equation(r"d = \sqrt{(2-1)^2 + (1-3)^2} = \sqrt5")

request: does a quarter-turn rotation have any eigenvectors?

beats.intent: A grid with three vectors pointing different ways
beats.narration: Take a few vectors pointing in different directions.
beats.code:
stage.title("A rotation has no eigenvectors")
p = draw_plane(stage)
vs = [draw_vector(stage, p, xy, color=c) for xy, c in (((2, 0), YELLOW), ((1, 1), GREEN), ((-1, 2), BLUE))]

beats.intent: The quarter-turn [[0, -1], [1, 0]] applied, every vector knocked off its line
beats.narration: Turn the plane a quarter turn. Every vector swings to a new direction: none stays on its own line.
beats.code: apply_matrix(stage, p, [[0, -1], [1, 0]], riders=vs)

beats.intent: The grid beside λ^2 + 1 = 0, no real solution
beats.narration: The stretch factors would have to solve lambda squared plus one equals zero, which has no real answer.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\lambda^2 + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \pm i")

request: what is the vector equation of a line?

beats.intent: A grid with the point a = (1, 1) and a direction arrow d = (2, 1) from it
beats.narration: A line through the point one, one heading in the direction two, one.
beats.code:
stage.title("r = a + t d")
p = draw_plane(stage)
a = mark_point(stage, p, (1, 1), color=RED, label="a")
d = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(1, 1), p.c2p(3, 2))
stage.label(d, "d", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Points for t = -1, 0, 0.5, 1 marked along the line
beats.narration: Step t times along d: t equals minus one, zero, a half and one give points on the line.
beats.code:
for t in (-1, 0, 0.5, 1):
    mark_point(stage, p, (1 + 2 * t, 1 + t), color=GREEN, label=f"t={t}")

beats.intent: The whole line drawn through them beside r = (1, 1) + t(2, 1)
beats.narration: Every value of t gives a point, and together they make the line.
beats.code:
line = draw_line(stage, p.c2p(-3, -1), p.c2p(4, 2.5), color=BLUE)
stage.equation(r"r = \begin{bmatrix}1\\1\end{bmatrix} + t\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}")
